title: The President of India
simple: India will have a President. The President is the head of the country.

questions.q: Who is the head of the Indian State?
Which Article states that there shall be a President of India?
Who is the formal constitutional head of the Republic of India?

title: Election of the President
simple: The President is chosen by elected MPs of both Houses of Parliament and elected MLAs of the States (and Delhi & Puducherry). Citizens do not vote directly.

questions.q: Do citizens directly vote to elect the President?
Who among the following does NOT vote in the Presidential election?
Which union territories participate in the election of the President?

title: Term of the President
simple: The President holds office for 5 years.

questions.q: What is the term of the President?
To whom does the President address their letter of resignation?
Can a person be re-elected as President of India after completing a 5-year term?

title: Who can become President
simple: To become President you must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a Lok Sabha member.

questions.q: Minimum age to become President?
To qualify as President, a candidate must be qualified for election as a member of which body?
Which citizenship requirement is set for the President of India?
options: Citizen residing in India for 20 years

title: Impeachment of the President
simple: Parliament can remove the President for violating the Constitution through a process called impeachment.

questions.q: The process to remove the President is called?
On what sole ground can the President of India be impeached under Article 61?
In which House of Parliament can an impeachment charge against the President be initiated?

title: Pardoning power of the President
simple: The President can pardon, reduce or suspend the punishment of a convicted person, including a death sentence.

questions.q: Which Article gives the President power to pardon?
Does the President have the power to grant pardon in cases of punishment by a Court Martial?
The power to commute or pardon a sentence of death is exclusively vested in:

title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
simple: A Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister advises the President. The President appoints the PM, and the ministers are together answerable to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to?
Who advises the President in the exercise of constitutional functions?
options: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister

questions.q: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of whom?

title: Attorney General of India
simple: The Attorney General is the top lawyer of the Government of India and gives it legal advice.

questions.q: Who is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India?
Who appoints the Attorney General of India under Article 76?
Does the Attorney General have the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament?
options: Yes, but without the right to vote

title: Parliament
simple: Parliament is made of three parts: the President, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

questions.q: Is the President a part of Parliament?
How many constituent parts form the Parliament of India?
options: Four (President, PM, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha)

questions.q: What is the upper house of the Indian Parliament officially called in the Constitution?

title: Rajya Sabha
simple: Rajya Sabha can have up to 250 members. 12 are nominated by the President for their knowledge of art, science, literature or social service.

questions.q: How many Rajya Sabha members are nominated by the President?
Which field is NOT one of the criteria for President nominations to Rajya Sabha under Article 80?
What is the maximum constitutional strength of the Rajya Sabha?

title: Duration of the Houses
simple: Lok Sabha lasts 5 years unless dissolved earlier. Rajya Sabha is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every 2 years.

questions.q: Which House can never be dissolved?
What fraction of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years?
What is the normal duration of the Lok Sabha from the date of its first meeting?

title: Money Bills
simple: A Money Bill (about taxes and government money) can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha can only suggest changes within 14 days.

questions.q: Where can a Money Bill be introduced?
Within how many days must Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to Lok Sabha?
Who decides definitively whether a bill is a Money Bill or not?

title: Joint Sitting
simple: If the two Houses disagree on an ordinary bill, the President can call both Houses to meet together and vote.

questions.q: Who calls a joint sitting of Parliament?
Who presides over a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
Can a Joint Sitting be called for a Money Bill?
options: No, Money Bills have no joint sitting
Only if Rajya Sabha rejects it

title: Ordinances
simple: When Parliament is not in session, the President can make a temporary law called an Ordinance if urgently needed.

questions.q: A temporary law made by the President when Parliament is not in session is?
An Ordinance promulgated by the President must be approved by Parliament within how long after reassembly?
Under what primary condition can the President promulgate an Ordinance?
options: At least one House is not in session and immediate action is required

title: Supreme Court
simple: India has a Supreme Court with a Chief Justice and other judges. Supreme Court judges retire at 65.

questions.q: Retirement age of a Supreme Court judge?
Who appoints the judges of the Supreme Court of India?
Where is the principal seat of the Supreme Court of India established by Article 130?

title: Supreme Court decisions bind all courts
simple: The law declared by the Supreme Court must be followed by all courts in India.

questions.q: Supreme Court judgments are binding on?
According to Article 141, the law declared by Supreme Court is binding on:
options: All courts within the territory of India

questions.q: The principle of binding precedent under Article 141 is based on which legal doctrine?

title: Advisory opinion
simple: The President can ask the Supreme Court for its opinion on an important question of law or fact.

questions.q: Who can seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion?
Is the advisory opinion given by the Supreme Court under Article 143 binding on the President?
options: No, it is advisory in nature

questions.q: Under Article 143, on what matters can the President consult the Supreme Court?
options: Questions of law or fact of public importance

title: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
simple: The CAG checks (audits) how the government spends public money.

questions.q: Who audits government spending?
Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
To whom does the CAG submit audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union?

title: Governor of a State
simple: Each State has a Governor, appointed by the President.

What is the minimum age required to be appointed as Governor of a State?

title: Pardoning power of the Governor
simple: The Governor can pardon or reduce punishments for offences against State laws (but cannot pardon a death sentence).

questions.q: Can a Governor pardon a death sentence?
Can a Governor pardon a sentence of death given under state law?
options: No, only the President has death sentence pardoning power

simple: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister. The CM leads the State Council of Ministers, which is responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

The State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:

title: State Legislature
simple: Each State has a Legislature with the Governor and a Legislative Assembly (some also have a Legislative Council). An Assembly has between 60 and 500 members.

What is the minimum number of members in a State Legislative Assembly as per Article 170 (subject to exceptions)?
What is the upper house of a State Legislature called where it exists?

title: High Courts
simple: Each State has a High Court. High Court judges retire at 62.

questions.q: Retirement age of a High Court judge?
Who appoints the Chief Justice and judges of a High Court?
To whom does a High Court judge address their resignation letter?
options: The Chief Justice of High Court

title: Writ power of High Courts
simple: High Courts can issue orders called writs to protect your Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.

simple: District Judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.
